This is a risk-layer event, not an earnings event. The more pressing concern for this committee is the valuation gap: our base-case intrinsic value is approximately $200/share, and the stock trades at $421 — a 110% premium that requires sustained double-digit Optum growth and benign medical cost trends to justify. The probe adds a discount-rate headwind at exactly the wrong time. I recommend holding current position without adding, and investigating three things before the next decision point: (1) the full scope of DOJ's theory of harm in the Claritev probe; (2) management's Q2 commentary on the investigation's status and strategic contingency plans; and (3) whether the deteriorating gross margin trend (24.6% to 18.5% over four years) reflects cyclical MCR noise or a structural reset of the earnings algorithm. This judgment would be proven wrong if the DOJ probe is resolved without enforcement action, Optum sustains double-digit revenue growth organically, and medical cost ratios stabilize — in that scenario the risk premium is unwarranted and the moat assessment improves.
